findings.text: The new audit_ran invariant is bypassed by this function's own except branch, on an input the node's test does not construct. Triggering input: any exception from reconcile_attachment_consistency - e.g. gc.query raising RuntimeError('graph unavailable') during a rename. Measured against the landed code: gate_migrated_attachments(gc, sn_id='electron_density') -> audit_ran True, '== AttachmentAuditResult()' True, _attachment_violation_rows(result) -> [] , as_dict()['audit_ran'] True. An audit that raised is therefore serialised as a clean, fully audited, all-zero receipt - the exact defect this node closed for the scoped bypass. The fix is one keyword: return AttachmentAuditResult(audit_ran=False) in the except branch (the fail-open return itself is correct and must stay, per its docstring). Latent today because the function has no production caller; it becomes live the moment it is rewired to a reporting path. It also falsifies the landed evidence sentence 'defaults to true, preserving the meaning of every existing construction site'.

test_gate_survives_a_graph_failure asserts 'result == AttachmentAuditResult()' for the exception fallback above, so the suite now actively pins 'an audit that did not run equals a clean audit' as correct behaviour. Any later attempt to set audit_ran=False on that path turns this green test red and reads as a regression. The assertion should be narrowed to the fields it means (no detachments, no rejections) plus 'result.audit_ran is False'. Outside this node's write scope, reported not fixed.

Systemic, and fenced out of this node: the shared _global_maintenance_call helper returns the caller-supplied default (usually {}) when skip_global_maintenance is True, with no log line and no not-run marker, and nine sibling maintenance passes go through it (lines 1679, 1693, 1720, 1739, 1765, 1780, 1793, 1806, 1828). Triggering input: sn run with the scoped-maintenance bypass - the provenance reconcile, vocab-gap reconcile, unit reconcile, catalog-status reconcile and the rest each report an empty result indistinguishable from 'ran and found nothing'. This node fixed one instance of the class; the receipt belongs in the shared helper. Reported as a follow-on, not a defect in this change.

Not a defect - the caller analysis the gate asked for, recorded so it is not re-derived. _attachment_violation_rows has exactly ONE caller, _reconcile_recovery_consistency at provenance_rebuild.py:535, which can now raise ValueError where it previously returned a list. Its only caller is rebuild_provenance at line 725, inside a try/finally whose finally only closes the GraphClient - there is no except there, and the only except clauses in the whole module are two OSError handlers and one yaml.YAMLError handler in unrelated git/yaml helpers, so NOTHING catches this broadly and nothing swallows it. rebuild_provenance has no production caller in the repository (catalog_reconcile.py imports only bind_recovery_sources and recovery_sources_from_entries; there is no CLI entry point), so the new raise changes no live behaviour today. Both values that actually reach the function - the dry-run reconcile result and audit_attachments(gc=gc) - always carry audit_ran=True, which is also why the mocked tests that return a bare AttachmentAuditResult() stayed green.

justifications.durability: The pin fires and the mutation proof is real, but the invariant the field introduces is not established at every construction site, and an existing test pins the violation green. Demonstrated in this reviewer's worktree against the landed code: with gc.query raising RuntimeError('graph unavailable'), gate_migrated_attachments(gc, sn_id='electron_density') returns audit_ran=True, compares == AttachmentAuditResult(), and _attachment_violation_rows(result) returns [] - the exact suppression this node closed, one call site away, on an input the node's test does not construct. tests/standard_names/test_attachment_audit.py:3202 asserts 'result == AttachmentAuditResult()' for that path, so the audit-did-not-run-equals-clean equivalence is now actively pinned by the suite. It is latent rather than live only because gate_migrated_attachments currently has no production caller (grep finds it referenced only from tests, and test_attachment_audit.py:1050 asserts the refine path does NOT call it); it becomes a live fail-open the moment that gate is rewired to anything that reports. The new test itself is good: removing audit_ran=False fails it by name at 'assert bypassed.audit_ran is False'.
justifications.evidence: Every log the node cited was opened and matches. defect-reproduction.log prints skipped_equals_clean=True, same_receipt=True and both log gates false, with two byte-identical all-zero receipts - that is the defect, reproduced before repair rather than asserted. negative-control.log is well formed: its first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim ('Set the scoped bypass result back to default audit_ran=True by removing audit_ran=False from its AttachmentAuditResult construction.') and it ends '1 failed' exit 1 on the new test by name. focused-after.log ends '72 passed, 15 deselected' exit 0. The suite delta checks arithmetically: base 509a4703d '20 failed, 7497 passed, 8 skipped, 326 deselected ... 3 errors' and head '20 failed, 7498 passed, 8 skipped, 326 deselected ... 3 errors' - 20+3=23 failure ids, the two id lists in the manifest are identical, and passed moves by exactly the one test added. Docked: the fail-closed half of the change is evidenced only by a direct call to a private function. _attachment_violation_rows has exactly one caller and that caller's caller has no production caller in the repo, so no log shows the raise reaching anything, and the evidence record does not say so.
justifications.fit: The change follows the module's idiom - mechanism-named helpers (_log_attachment_audit_result, _run_attachment_audit_for_pool_run), function-local imports, docstrings that state the rule, and no plan, sprint or ticket label in source or commit. The extraction is behaviour-preserving on the audited path: the log predicate is still 'result.detached or result.rejected', the call keeps run_id=run_id through asyncio.to_thread, and the discarded return value is safe because grep shows no remaining reference to attach_result in loop.py. Inserting audit_ran as the FIRST dataclass field is safe here - a repo-wide grep finds zero positional constructions of AttachmentAuditResult - though it is the kind of ordering change that would silently rebind a positional argument. Docked twice. First, loop.py already owns a shared skip idiom, _global_maintenance_call (loop.py:1612), which nine other maintenance passes use and which returns the caller's default silently with no receipt at all; this node built a second, parallel skip idiom beside it rather than extending it, so the module now has two ways to skip and only one of them says so. Second, both new helpers are annotated 'Any' rather than AttachmentAuditResult, which is the one type the field depends on.

The goal — a skipped attachment audit must not read as a clean one — is met on the named path and was verified here rather than taken from the report. At the integrated head (d24da5905d7afae4bd049d5b3c753d550b9ebe8b, both commits ancestors of HEAD 032fa5d87) the scoped bypass constructs AttachmentAuditResult(audit_ran=False), the pool loop emits 'attachment-consistency audit skipped - skip_global_maintenance=True', and _attachment_violation_rows raises on that value; tests/standard_names/test_skipped_audit_is_visible.py and tests/standard_names/test_attachment_audit.py::test_gate_survives_a_graph_failure return 2 passed exit 0 in this reviewer's worktree.
